evidence: establish() (web/stage/src/net/useGame.ts:324-330) creates `new GameClient({... onState})`, assigns `clientRef.current = client` (L329), and NEVER closes the prior ref. The ONLY .close() call is in the unmount cleanup (L369); there is no `prev?.close()` on reconnect. The `onState` closure is defined once (L150-158) and reused for every client (passed at L327); it does NOT check `client === clientRef.current`. In client.ts, handleClose() (L101-104) returns early only if `this.closed`, and `this.closed` is set solely by close() (L88). Since the old client is never close()d, its `this.closed` stays false, so a late handleClose fires `onState(false)`. connect() (client.ts:56-57) wires TWO close paths — `readLoop(...).catch(handleClose)` and `wt.closed.then(handleClose)` — plus readLoop's normal `done` -> handleClose (L138). REACHABILITY: two sub-cases. (1) UNCONDITIONAL LEAK: on every reconnect the prior GameClient's WebTransport + writer + pending `wt.closed` handler are orphaned (never closed) — this is certain, not timing-dependent. (2) SPURIOUS-RECONNECT CHURN (timing-dependent): if the server closes only the bidi control stream while the QUIC session lingers, readLoop gets `done` at t=0 -> onState(false) -> scheduleReconnect (L157) -> new client live by ~t+500ms. When the session finally closes later, the OLD client's `wt.closed` resolves -> handleClose -> onState(false) on a healthy link -> scheduleReconnect (L139-148: guard `reconnectTimer!==null || establishing` is clear on an idle-healthy link, so it fires) -> establish() spawns a THIRD client, overwriting clientRef and orphaning the healthy one. The common full-session-drop double-fire (readLoop done + wt.closed together) is HARMLESS because the second onState(false) hits the reconnectTimer!=null guard; harm needs the late-after-reconnect variant, which requires stream-close-without-session-close. That path is plausible under WebTransport but not guaranteed, so the churn is real-but-narrow while the leak is unconditional.
fix: In establish(), close the superseded client before overwriting: `const prev = clientRef.current; clientRef.current = client; void prev?.close();` (setting the prior client's this.closed=true so its late handleClose is suppressed). Do it right at L329.
fix_risk: low — close() is idempotent and swallows errors (client.ts:87-99); the fresh client is already assigned so no live link is torn down.

evidence: Same root defect, worse blast radius. establish() (web/mobile/src/lib/useGame.ts:271-320) is guarded by `if (clientRef.current) return` (L273), assigns `clientRef.current = client` (L293), and never close()s a prior client. handleDisconnect() (L261-269) — the SHARED callback invoked by ANY client's onState(false) via the closure at L284-291 — only does `clientRef.current = null` (L265), never close(). The onState closure does NOT check which client fired it. Per client.ts handleClose() (L101-104), the nulled-but-not-closed old client keeps this.closed=false and CAN still fire onState(false) from its pending wt.closed. REACHABILITY: (1) UNCONDITIONAL LEAK — every reconnect orphans the old client's transport + pending wt.closed handler. (2) LIVE TEARDOWN (timing-dependent): old client onState(false) -> handleDisconnect nulls ref + scheduleReconnect (L268) -> reconnect fires (L249-253, guard `unmountedRef || clientRef.current` clear) -> new client connects, startHeartbeat (L317), conn:connected. When the OLD client's session closes late, its wt.closed -> handleClose -> onState(false) -> shared handleDisconnect runs against LIVE state: stopHeartbeat() kills the live heartbeat (L262), clientRef.current=null drops the LIVE client WITHOUT closing it (now the new client leaks too, L265), conn flips to 'disconnected', scheduleReconnect spawns yet another socket -> transient duplicate socket for the same deviceFP/handle. As in s2-ui-01, the common same-drop double-fire is neutralized by the reconnectTimerRef guard (L245); harm needs the late-wt.closed-after-reconnect variant. MITIGATION: server-side deviceFP dedup (per MEMORY / §3.2 resume) blunts SCORE loss, but connection churn, a live-user momentary disconnect, duplicate-connection anti-cheat noise, and the client leak remain — hence medium not high.
fix: In handleDisconnect, close the ref instead of just nulling: `const prev = clientRef.current; clientRef.current = null; void prev?.close();` (L265). This sets prev.closed=true so any late duplicate onState from it is suppressed by handleClose's `if (this.closed) return`. Optionally also guard the onState closure to ignore firings from a client that is no longer clientRef.current.
fix_risk: low — close() is idempotent/error-swallowing; nulling already happened here so no behavioral regression beyond suppressing the stale callback.

evidence: Confirmed the try/catch boundary: in establish() (web/mobile/src/lib/useGame.ts:279-305) the try wraps ONLY fetchCertHashes, `new GameClient`, wireHandlers, and `await client.connect()`. The catch (L296-305) nulls clientRef and scheduleReconnect()s. Past the catch — `await client.send(hello)` (L309-312), `await client.send(resync)` (L314), and `startHeartbeat()` (L317) — is UNGUARDED. establish is invoked via `void establish(...)` (connect L327-330 and establishRef L323-324), so a post-connect send rejection IS an unhandled promise rejection — CONFIRMED, and it re-introduces exactly the uistage-5 class hardened elsewhere (heartbeat catches at L109-113). THAT part is a real defect. HOWEVER the 'permanent wedge that only luck unsticks' claim is OVERSTATED. For the wedge to persist you need writer.write to reject WHILE the read side never surfaces a close and wt.closed never resolves. But client.connect (client.ts:56-57) wires `readLoop(...).catch(() => handleClose())` and `wt.closed.then(handleClose)`; a transport/stream error that fails a write almost always also errors the reader or resolves wt.closed -> handleClose -> onState(false) -> handleDisconnect() -> recovery. The synchronous `throw new Error('not connected')` path (client.ts:76) can't fire here because connect() sets this.writer before resolving. So the wedge requires write-fails-but-read-and-session-stay-open — a narrow, largely theoretical transport state, not the routine outcome the finding implies. Net: unhandled rejection is real (low severity, cosmetic/log-noise + a brief no-heartbeat window); permanent wedge is not reliably reachable.
fix: Wrap the post-connect hello/resync/startHeartbeat (L309-317) in a try/catch that on failure does `clientRef.current = null; scheduleReconnect(); return;` — mirroring the connect() catch. Prefer closing first: `void client.close(); clientRef.current = null;`.
fix_risk: low — purely additive error handling; on the success path behavior is unchanged.

evidence: web/stage/src/views/Board.tsx destructures `{ rows, cols, cells } = board` (L11) with no clamp. Both the category loop (L20-30: `for col 1..cols` nested `for r 1..rows`) and the render (L47-49: `Array.from({ length: rows }).map(... Array.from({ length: cols }).map(...))`) use dimensions directly. `cells ?? []` (L15) only guards a missing/non-array cells list, NOT absurd dimensions — CONFIRMED, exactly as claimed. Mechanism is real: rows=cols=50000 -> the inner map materializes ~2.5e9 React elements synchronously during render -> OOM/hang. An OOM tab-crash or a synchronous hang is NOT a thrown error, so the React ErrorBoundary cannot catch it — defeating the 'malformed board frame must never freeze the projector' intent already documented in the L13-15 comment. Note negative/NaN/non-integer dims are benign (Array.from({length:-1|NaN}) -> []), so only large positive integers are the threat. SEVERITY = LOW and honestly bounded: the ONLY frame source is the trusted server (security model: server is trusted; mobile is the hostile party and never sends board frames). The cited threat is a server BUG or corrupt/garbage frame, not an attacker-controlled path — so this is defensive hardening consistent with the existing `cells ?? []` guard, not an exploitable DoS.
fix: Clamp before use: `const rows = Math.max(0, Math.min(board.rows | 0, 12)); const cols = Math.max(0, Math.min(board.cols | 0, 12));` (12 is a sane Jeopardy-board ceiling; pick the real max from protocol). Use the clamped values in both the category loop and the render.
fix_risk: low — clamp only bites on out-of-spec frames; legitimate boards are well under any sane cap.
